solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Silly notice rejected by paper (4)

indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the letters of AD run the other way

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, as in the small ads

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at a foolish announcement the newspaper refused to print.
annotation.walkthrough: FT is the usual crossword shorthand for the Financial Times, the pink British business paper.
annotation.definitionFit: Daft is everyday British for silly or foolish.

entries.clue: Careful editor coming up with release (10)

indicatorNotes.coming up: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom, so ED turns to DE

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

annotation.surface: A meticulous editor arrives bringing a press release.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like a noun, a press release, but it is the verb, to set free.
annotation.definitionFit: A deliberate action is careful and considered rather than hasty.

entries.clue: Fine coffee on new level (7)

blocks.note: f = fine, as on pencil grades
a latte is a milky coffee

annotation.surface: Someone praises a good coffee served at a new floor of a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Level' reads as a noun, a storey, but it is the verb, to make flat; 'on' just places the coffee above N in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: levelling a lawn or a building leaves it flat.

entries.clue: Expert entertaining church playing Bliss is easy to follow (10)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertaining guests holds them inside

annotation.surface: A skilled musician at a church performs a piece by the composer Arthur Bliss, which listeners find easy to take in.
annotation.walkthrough: The expert is split to take the church and the shuffled letters inside. Bliss looks like a composer's name here (Arthur Bliss was a Master of the Queen's Music), but it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: writing or music that is easy to follow can be approached by anyone, without special knowledge.

entries.clue: Deception foolish cuddle ended (9)

indicatorNotes.foolish: a foolish arrangement is a muddled one, so the letters of CUDDLE are jumbled

annotation.surface: A lover's trick ends a silly embrace.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a short, sour romance; the definition sits at the far end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a meeting that has concluded has come to its close.

entries.clue: Rows of bushes ignoring height limits (5)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: ignoring the H leaves it out

annotation.surface: Rows of shrubs are planted with no regard for how tall they may grow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Height limits' reads as one phrase about hedge heights; the definition is 'limits' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the outer boundaries of a field or a town mark where it stops.

entries.clue: Part about very quiet artist with constant nervous action revealing fraud? (5,8)

indicatorNotes.about: SHARE goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: pp = pianissimo, very quietly in music
c is the constant for the speed of light
a tic is a nervous twitch

annotation.surface: A timid painter's nervous twitching gives away that they are a fake.
annotation.walkthrough: The part opens up to hold the other four pieces in order. The question mark marks 'fraud' as an example: sharp practice is sly dishonesty, of which fraud is one kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest or barely legal dealing, so fraud is an instance of it.

entries.clue: Spoke proudly, sad to be struggling (7)

indicatorNotes.to be struggling: letters struggling are thrashing about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone brags despite being unhappy about having a hard time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To be' does double duty in the surface: part of the phrase 'sad to be struggling', but its letters belong to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To boast is to speak proudly of oneself.

entries.clue: Test, complex, amended in part (4)

indicatorNotes.in part: the answer is part of the words around it

blocks.note: the last three letters of 'complex' and the first two of 'amended'

annotation.surface: A complicated test has been partly revised.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the comma between 'complex' and 'amended'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a school or university examination is a formal test of knowledge.

entries.clue: Storyteller mostly lives on in secretive affair (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so LIAR loses its last letter

blocks.note: a liar tells stories; LIAR minus its last letter
to be, to exist: he is, he lives

annotation.surface: A novelist carries on writing, deep in a secret romance.
annotation.walkthrough: A storyteller in crosswords is often a liar, one who tells stories.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: borrowed from French, the word is used for an illicit love affair kept hidden.

entries.clue: Role star played, entertaining old emperor eventually (6,2,5)

indicatorNotes.played: the letters of ROLE STAR are played about with
indicatorNotes.entertaining: the rearranged letters hold ONERO inside

annotation.surface: An actor in a part eventually takes on the role of an ancient emperor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Role star played' reads as an actor's part; 'star' is only letters for the mix, and 'old' is the usual single O.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase says a thing will happen at some unspecified future time, which is what eventually says in one word.

entries.clue: Excellent area surrounding a city in Spain (7)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround something is to enclose it, so the first word's letters go around the next

annotation.surface: A fine district encircles a Spanish city.
annotation.walkthrough: GRAN(A)D takes the clue's 'a', then area's A goes on the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra.

entries.clue: Recalled Maxim interrupting worship with hint about abyss (10,3)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: called back, so MOTTO is read backwards
indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in on something, so the reversed maxim sits in the middle of the worship word
indicatorNotes.about: about as in 'about turn', a word facing the other way

blocks.note: to bless is to praise or worship

annotation.surface: Someone remembers a saying that broke into their prayers, along with a clue about a chasm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' looks like remembered, but here it means called back, turned around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an abyss is a hole so deep it seems to have no floor.

entries.clue: Characteristic energy put into studies in review affected by financial constraints (10)

indicatorNotes.put into: what is put into something ends up inside it
indicatorNotes.in review: looked back over, so DENS is read backwards

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

annotation.surface: A report says typical vigour is being channelled into academic studies under review because money is tight.
annotation.walkthrough: S(TRAIT E)NED. 'Studies' reads as academic work, but it is the plural of study, the room: a den.
annotation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are those of hardship, short of money.

entries.clue: Country house short of good variety (5)

indicatorNotes.short of: lacking, so the G is dropped

blocks.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

annotation.surface: A rural mansion lacks a decent selection.
annotation.walkthrough: A grange is a British country house, often an old farmhouse with its outbuildings.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shop's wide selection of goods can be described either way.

entries.clue: Record florid appeal? Rubbish (9)

annotation.surface: Someone dismisses an overblown plea on a record as worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as a noun, but it is the British verb, to criticise as worthless. IT for sex appeal is an old convention.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquial verb: rubbishing a theory means pouring scorn on it until nobody believes it.

entries.clue: Rigorous line followed by medical department (9)

annotation.surface: Strict protocol is followed by a hospital department.
annotation.walkthrough: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat, a staple of crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tough safety checks that allow no slack are described with both words.

entries.clue: Story involving nobleman and king in difficult task (4,5)

annotation.surface: A legend in which a lord and a king undertake a hard quest.
annotation.walkthrough: TAL(LORD)E, then R.
annotation.definitionFit: A tall order is a demand that is hard to meet.

entries.clue: Behave aggressively in Los Angeles and yell (4,3)

annotation.surface: Someone acts up and yells on the streets of LA.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link here, not a container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: a cornered animal or an angry person suddenly strikes out, physically or in words.

entries.clue: Land force not available (5)

blocks.note: chi (qi) is the life force in Chinese thought

annotation.surface: An army cannot be deployed on the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land force' reads as an army; split it, and 'Land' is the definition and 'force' the life force CHI.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular country, and land is a common crossword word for any nation.

entries.clue: Passivity during irate rioting (7)

indicatorNotes.rioting: the letters of IRATE run riot into a new order

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the war'

annotation.surface: Some stand by doing nothing while angry crowds riot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pits the idle against the furious, which is exactly the answer's contrast.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from physics: a body at rest stays at rest, as a passive person does.

entries.clue: Send client off newly assured (4-9)

indicatorNotes.newly: the letters are made anew, in a new order

annotation.surface: A professional dismisses a customer, feeling freshly sure of themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like part of 'send off', but its letters are fodder too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an assured performer trusts their own abilities.

entries.clue: Load vehicle and set off (5)

blocks.note: to go is to set off

annotation.surface: Pack up the car and start the journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Load' reads as a verb, but the answer is the noun: a load carried.
annotation.definitionFit: Cargo is a load carried by a ship or vehicle.

entries.clue: Plans raised for unsolicited messages (4)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting means reading upwards

blocks.note: maps are plans, as in a street plan

annotation.surface: Schemes are drawn up to deal with junk mail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plans' reads as schemes, but it means maps; 'raised' reverses them in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A modern sense: junk email sent in bulk took its name from the tinned meat, via a Monty Python sketch.

entries.clue: Fortune spent in the end to charge a conspirator (7)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the end of 'spent' is taken
indicatorNotes.to charge: LOT and T charge, or fill, PER

blocks.note: a = per, as in £5 a head

annotation.surface: A fortune has been squandered, and in the end a schemer is to be charged.
annotation.walkthrough: P(LOT T)ER. 'A' is the hardest piece: it means PER, each. 'Charge' looks legal, but it means fill, as you charge a glass.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who hatches a secret scheme with others, like Guy Fawkes.

entries.clue: Football team always working to contain opposition’s No 7 (7)

indicatorNotes.to contain: EVER ON holds the T inside

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

annotation.surface: A football side keeps working to mark the other team's number 7 player.
annotation.walkthrough: EVER(T)ON. 'No 7' looks like a shirt number, but it counts letters. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League football team.

entries.clue: Doctor backed nonsense by opening speaker going on and on (10)

indicatorNotes.backed: sent backwards, so ROT becomes TOR

annotation.surface: A physician supported some drivel from an opening speaker who wouldn't stop talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening speaker' looks like the first to speak; split it, and 'opening' gives MOUTH while 'speaker' starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A motormouth is someone who talks incessantly.

entries.clue: Gang not allowed in hearing (4)

indicatorNotes.in hearing: what is heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.surface: A gang is barred from a court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session, but it signals the sound of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a band of robbers or rebels is a gang of them.
